title: CERT-In Vulnerability Note  CIVN-2026-0542
content:
CERT-In Vulnerability Note 
                                                                      CIVN-2026-0542
Authentication Bypass Vulnerability in OpenSSH
Original Issue Date:November  06, 2026
Severity Rating: CRITICAL
Software Affected
OpenSSH versions prior to 10.6p2
Overview
A vulnerability has been reported in OpenSSH which could allow a remote attacker to bypass password authentication mechanism on the targeted system.
Target Audience:
All organizations and individuals using OpenSSH.
Risk Assessment:
High risk of service disruption.
Impact Assessment:
Potential for High risk of denial of service (DoS) conditions.
Description
OpenSSH is a SSH protocol 2.0 implementation and includes sftp client and server support.
This vulnerability exists in OpenSSH due to authentication bypass. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending an unusually long password to the targeted system running OpenSSH on Linux with musl libc and PAM disabled.
Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to gain unauthorized access and elevate privileges on the targeted system.
Solution
Apply appropriate updates as mentioned by the vendor:
https://www.openssh.org/txt/release-10.6p2
Vendor Information
OpenSSH
https://www.openssh.org/
References
